need to fix compilation errors. The test class imports JUnit4 and JUnit5, Mockito, etc. In this environment, likely only JUnit4 is available, and no Mockito. To simplify, we can remove Mockito usage and replace with simple stub implementations. Also remove annotations that need those imports.

We can rewrite test class to use only JUnit4 (org.junit.*) and no Mockito. Use simple stub indicator for all tests. Remove @Mock, reset, verify, when, verifyNoMoreInteractions. Instead manually simulate behavior.

Simplify: In setupBeforeEach, create a stub indicator that returns a known value for getValue, and return series, unstable bars etc. Or we can just test using the stub indicator directly, not need mock.

Also remove @ExtendWith and @RunWith. Use @RunWith(JUnit4.class) maybe not needed. JUnit4 default runner.

Also BaseBarBuilder is not public; use Bar.builder? In ta4j, there is BarBuilder maybe accessible via org.ta4j.core.BarBuilder? But we can avoid building series using BaseBarSeriesBuilder and adding simple bars using series.addBar(series.barBuilder().time(...).openPrice...?). Simpler: use BaseBarSeriesBuilder and then add bars using series.addBar(new org.ta4j.core.BaseBar(...)). However BaseBar constructor may be public. Let's check typical usage: new BaseBar(Duration.ofDays(1), ZonedDateTime..., open, high, low, close, volume). Might be complex. To avoid series usage, we can create a minimal BarSeries using BaseBarSeriesBuilder with no bars, and only need for getBarSeries test. That test expects getBarSeries returns series. We can set mockIndicator.getBarSeries to return series, but without mock we can create a custom stub indicator that returns series.

Define a StubIndicator that takes Num fixedValue, BarSeries barSeries, int unstableBars. Implement getValue, getBarSeries, getUnstableBars accordingly.

Then in each test, instantiate numericIndicator = NumericIndicator.of(stub). No need for @BeforeEach.

Simplify test class: remove all Mockito related code, use plain JUnit4 tests.

Also remove main method (optional) but can keep.

Also need to import necessary classes: org.junit.Test, org.junit.Before, org.junit.BeforeClass, org.junit.After, org.junit.Assert.*.

Remove imports for Mockito and JUnit5.

Now ensure NumericIndicator.of exists. It returns NumericIndicator. We need to import NumericIndicator class.

Make sure to reference NumericIndicator delegate method; assume exists.

Implement tests accordingly.
